title: Compact surface skeletons and interactive gesture guides for console
creator: Martin Chen
description: Problem: Dashboard canvas and small-metric rails suffer inconsistent density and affordance across breakpoints, leading to visual noise in cost and rollout views. Purpose: Deliver a compact surface skeleton component family and a set of lightweight interactive gesture guides (onboarding / hover/focus patterns) that standardize spacing, focus states, and animation timing for dense metric lists and sparkline tiles. Scope: 1) token recommendations for compact spacing, elevation, and motion specific to compact surfaces; 2) Figma component library (variants + auto-layout) for compact cards, rails, and microchips; 3) interactive prototypes demonstrating pull-to-reveal rollouts, hover affordances for cost drilldowns, and keyboard navigation for dense lists; 4) accessibility checklist and a short dev acceptance guide. Out of scope: full refactor of large dashboard canvases and chart rendering behavior (separate chart team follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma library published with compact variants and documented props; 2) interactive prototype (desktop + mobile) demonstrating 3 gesture patterns: pull-to-reveal rollout rail, hover-to-expand metric microcard, and keyboard-first focus ring transitions; 3) token table with recommended values for spacing, elevations, and motion durations + examples mapping to existing tokens; 4) design review sign-off from Product (Jill Ramirez) and Engineering (Rajat Singh); 5) engineering-ready redlines and a short implementation QA checklist.
decisions: Adopt 6-point column rhythm for compact grids (usable at min width 280px)
Prefer subtle elevation (level-1) + 0.04s motion for micro-interactions to keep perceived latency low
Use a single compact token set (compact-spacing-*) mapped to existing spacing tokens to avoid introducing new primitives
Prototype will use mocked cost data with realistic token-level truncation/ellipsis behaviors for labels
